headline: Budget 2026 locks Peppol for VAT e-invoicing; Exchange for Change publishes the first certified RVM list
executive_summary: This Monday-to-Monday week has two identification keeps, and neither is a new barcode statute. On 28 October, Budget 2026 published HMRC’s e-invoicing implementation roadmap: from 1 April 2029 VAT-registered persons, including public bodies, must issue and receive VAT invoices as structured e-invoices unless a specific exemption applies, and Peppol is the UK’s core interoperability framework. HMRC will take the UK Peppol Authority from NHS Supply Chain. Every user will need a business identifier as part of their Peppol participant identity; which identifiers the UK will accept is still unchosen and is due between October 2027 and April 2028. GS1 is not named, and GLN is not designated. A separate digital-reporting consultation, also opened on 28 October and closing on 20 January 2027, asks whether HMRC might later receive selected e-invoice data; it does not change the 2029 duty. On 29 October Exchange for Change published the first certified reverse-vending-machine list, independently assessed by PPS against 77 requirements that include identification and acceptance of eligible containers. The barcode rules themselves did not change. Construction produced no keep: MHCLG’s show-and-tells start on 5 November, after this window. Healthcare produced no keep: last week’s CE-recognition decision is not repeated, and GS1 is still not a GB UDI issuing entity. Product-identifier enforcement for EU distance-sale imports began on 1 November; HMRC has still published no UK-exporter note.
cross_sector_themes: Peppol is now the UK’s chosen e-invoicing network, but the identifier that will sit on a participant identity is still a 2027–28 decision, not a GS1 mandate
DRS return-point machines that must read scheme barcodes are now a published certified list; on-pack GTIN change, product-testing guidelines and Article List registration clocks did not move
UDI, implant cards, a construction-product identifier and Official Journal citation of EN 18239 and EN 18246 remain draft, discovery or outstanding
PID reporting for EU distance-sale imports is now a live customs duty from 1 November 2026; HMRC has still published no UK-exporter note

sector_overviews.headline: E-invoicing identifiers go on the Budget clock; the certified RVM list is finally out
sector_overviews.summary: Retail has both of this week’s keeps. The Budget 2026 e-invoicing roadmap is the bigger one: Peppol is locked as the interoperability framework, HMRC will become the UK Peppol Authority, and a business-identifier decision is promised between October 2027 and April 2028. That is a location-identifier file for every VAT-registered supplier, not a GTIN or barcode duty. Exchange for Change then published, on 29 October, the first certified reverse-vending-machine list after two reported delays, with independent PPS assessment against 77 requirements including identification of eligible containers. The RVM specification already requires those machines to read EAN-8, EAN-13 and UPC and to read 2D Data Matrix and QR codes, validating against the Scheme Article List. Product-testing guidelines remain ‘in due course’ on the FAQs. PID reporting for EU distance-sale imports became mandatory on 1 November; Irish Revenue published a temporary ‘PID not available’ tolerance until 31 January 2027, but HMRC has still issued no UK-exporter note and the Commission’s Annex B amendment is still outstanding. PackUK’s 2026/27 confirmed fees remain indicated by the end of November. Wales DRS logistics contracts are still unawarded.

sector_overviews.headline: No construction identifier keep; MHCLG’s first public show-and-tell is 5 November
sector_overviews.summary: Construction produced no item that passed the identifier test. Last week’s MHCLG Digital discovery blog is not repeated. Fortnightly open show-and-tells start on 5 November, after this window; watch that session for any identifier, data-carrier or library choice. The Building Safety Regulator invited evidence on the future of Part K and Approved Document K on 27 October; that is protection from falling, collision and impact, not a unique product identifier. The Manufacturers’ Information Hub remains at proof-of-concept complete / MVP in development. Government responses to the Construction Products Reform White Paper and the General Safety Requirement consultation are still indicated later in 2026. Official Journal citation of EN 18239 and EN 18246 has still not appeared; the Commission’s indicative timeline still places that decision in November 2026. The EU construction-product DPP delegated act remains indicated for Q2 2027.

sector_overviews.headline: No healthcare identifier keep; NHS Peppol Authority will move to HMRC, GB UDI is still the December SI
sector_overviews.summary: Healthcare produced no new UDI, implant-card or Scan4Safety keep. The Budget e-invoicing roadmap does, however, say that the UK Peppol Authority function currently sits within NHS Supply Chain and that HMRC will take it on; timing of that transfer is not yet determined. NHS trusts and their suppliers already exchange structured invoices on Peppol and already use GLN in NHS eProcurement; the roadmap does not designate GLN for the economy-wide mandate. Last week’s indefinite CE-recognition decision is not repeated. Unique device identifiers and implant cards remain on the UKCA pre-market statutory instrument, still indicated for December 2026 adoption and June 2027 force, subject to Parliament. GS1 is still not listed as a GB issuing entity. MHRA’s October Safety Roundup, MedSafetyWeek (2–8 November) and individual field-safety and medicines-recall notices did not pass the identifier test. The 17 September GS1 UK / PSC Scan4Safety report is not repeated. The ABHI / GS1 UK ‘Understanding GB UDI’ session remains listed for 27 November.

items.title: Budget 2026 e-invoicing roadmap locks in Peppol; UK business identifiers still unchosen
items.summary: On 28 October 2026 HMRC published the e-invoicing implementation roadmap at Budget 2026. From 1 April 2029 VAT-registered persons, including public bodies, must issue and receive VAT invoices as structured e-invoices unless a specific exemption applies. Peppol is the UK’s core interoperability framework and HMRC will become the UK Peppol Authority. Every user will need a business identifier as part of their Peppol participant identity; which identifiers the UK will support is still unchosen.
items.what_changed:
HM Revenue & Customs published ‘Roadmap for e-invoicing implementation’ on 28 October 2026, alongside a tax information and impact note and enabling-powers language for Finance Bill 2026-27. The Budget document confirms the roadmap. From 1 April 2029, VAT-registered persons – including public-sector bodies – will need to be able to issue and receive VAT invoices as e-invoices, unless a specific exemption applies. An e-invoice is defined as the exchange of structured invoice data directly between buyers’ and suppliers’ financial systems; PDFs, images, HTML emails and fax are explicitly not e-invoices.

As announced at Tax Update Day 2026 and restated here, the UK will adopt Peppol as the core interoperability framework. Organisations will typically connect through a certified Access Point provided by their software supplier. The UK Peppol Authority function currently sits within NHS Supply Chain; HMRC will take it on. The Finance Bill will confer the functions needed for HMRC to prepare to become the Authority. It is not yet determined when that transfer will take effect. Enabling powers come into force from Royal Assent of Finance Bill 2026-27, expected in spring 2027; secondary legislation setting the operational rules may not conclude until autumn 2028 or early 2029. The government will provide at least 12 months’ notice of the detailed requirements, and aims to publish them between October 2027 and April 2028, including scope, exclusions, standards, guidance, business identifiers and service-provider requirements. A public technical consultation on proposed UK e-invoicing standards is indicated for spring 2027. Digitally excluded VAT-registered persons are expected to have an exemption, with the process set out by April 2028. Existing EDI and legacy systems may continue alongside the framework, but businesses using them will also need to be capable of exchanging e-invoices through it; further guidance is indicated for autumn 2027.

The roadmap’s business-identifiers chapter says a business identifier acts as a digital address on the Peppol network and forms part of an organisation’s Peppol participant identity. All e-invoicing users will need to register one. Peppol supports a range of identifiers and countries choose which to support nationally. ‘As the UK does not have a single identifier that applies across all organisation types, consideration is being given to how different business identifiers could support a wide range of businesses and sectors.’ The decision on which identifiers will be accepted or supported is intended for publication between October 2027 and April 2028. Annex 2 lists business identifiers among Peppol Authority Specific Requirements, with VAT-registration numbers given as an example, not as the chosen scheme. A separate consultation on e-invoicing digital reporting opened the same day and closes at 23:59 on 20 January 2027. It explores whether HMRC might later receive selected e-invoice data. It does not introduce a reporting duty and does not change the 2029 e-invoicing requirement.
items.why_it_matters_to_gs1:
This is the week the already-watched e-invoicing mandate acquired a network, a national authority and an identifier decision-date, not a GS1 mandate. Structured invoice exchange is point 3 of the relevance test; Peppol is already how NHS eProcurement moves invoices, and GLN is already how many NHS organisations and suppliers identify themselves on that network. The roadmap says every user will need a business identifier as part of their Peppol participant identity, and that the UK still has to choose which identifiers to support. That is the opening. It is not a designation of GLN, GTIN, or any other GS1 key. The text gives VAT-registration numbers as an example of a PASR identifier. If GS1 UK treats 28 October as ‘GLN day’, it will over-claim. If it treats the file as colour until 2029, the October 2027–April 2028 decision will be taken around VAT numbers and company-registration numbers without a worked NHS-to-economy mapping.

Two traps sit in this week’s text. First, Peppol is the network, not the identifier. Members who already hold a GLN for NHS or GDSN work should keep it; they should not invent a second location number on the back of the Budget, and they should not assume the GLN they hold is the identifier HMRC will accept. Second, HMRC will not sit in the invoice flow and will not validate invoices in transit. The Peppol Authority is a governance function. The separate digital-reporting consultation is the place where HMRC might later see selected invoice data; it is not that decision. If GS1 UK does nothing, software providers and HMRC will design participant identity around identifiers they already hold at scale – VAT numbers first – and NHS trusts that already route on GLN will face a dual-identity problem when the economy-wide mandate arrives. If members do nothing, VAT-registered suppliers into retail, construction and the NHS will arrive at the spring 2027 standards consultation with no view on whether GLN should be an accepted Peppol identifier, and with catalogues that cannot be joined to a location identity. Do not reprint packs. Do put GLN on the table as an option that already works on the NHS Peppol network, stating plainly that this roadmap does not require it.

GTIN as the usual product line on a structured invoice, not a new on-pack duty
GDSN / productDNA as the catalogue feed that would sit behind invoice lines if buyers match on GTIN
affected_stakeholders: VAT-registered businesses, sole traders, partnerships, charities and public bodies that issue or receive VAT invoices

items.title: Exchange for Change publishes first certified RVM list after October delays
items.summary: On 29 October 2026 Exchange for Change published the first list of reverse-vending machines certified for the UK Deposit Return Scheme, after two reported delays in October. Independent assessment by PPS tests each machine against 77 requirements, including identification and acceptance of eligible containers. The on-pack barcode rules did not change. Product-testing guidelines for non-standard containers remain unpublished.
items.what_changed:
Exchange for Change published ‘Exchange For Change publishes first list of certified Reverse Vending Machines and Artwork Guidelines’ on 29 October 2026, with Newsletter 16 the same day. A nine-page PDF, last-modified on 30 October, lists certified machine families. Certification is an independent assessment by PPS against the Exchange for Change RVM specification. Each submitted machine is tested against 77 requirements covering identification and acceptance of eligible containers, fraud prevention, connectivity with scheme systems, accessibility, and secure handling of transaction data. The process remains open and the list will be updated as further machines are certified. The PDF states that certification confirms the machine meets the requirements; it does not guarantee performance, and retailers remain responsible for agreeing performance terms with their supplier.

The PDF groups certified families as TOMRA Essential, Flow Standalone, Flow Flexible and Flow Multifeed; RVM Systems X2, Mega (Bulk) and Proline; EcoVend Eco Series and X Series; Recyclever RVM 5; Envipco Compact, Flex and Optima; Sielaff SiCompact and SiVario; and Ripet Plast-C and R80, with named models under each family. letsrecycle, reporting the same day, lists those seven suppliers. Exchange for Change also published RVM Artwork Guidelines (PDF last-modified 29 October) setting approved branding, signage and consumer instructions for certified models, for use alongside a retailer’s own branding. Russell Davies, chief executive, said the list is intended to help retailers of all sizes make informed decisions ahead of the 1 October 2027 launch, and pointed to a grant scheme for eligible small independent retailers. The Federation of Independent Retailers said it would monitor the list and noted a £6,000 grant with an application process launching in January 2027; Exchange for Change FAQs still say full grant details will be published in due course.

The underlying barcode duty is unchanged. Scheme containers must still carry a barcode registered on the Scheme Article List, compliant with the GS1 General Specifications or equivalent. The February 2026 RVM specification, still the published hardware standard, requires machines to store the Article List, validate the barcode read, read barcodes at up to 30 degrees tilt with at least 99.5 per cent recognition of undamaged barcodes, read EAN-8, EAN-13 and UPC, and read 2D Data Matrix and QR codes. FAQs still say the product-testing process for non-standard container formats ‘will be published in due course’.
items.why_it_matters_to_gs1:
This is the week the already-watched certified RVM list became a public buying file, not a new GS1 mandate and not a change to on-pack GTIN allocation. Return-point machines are how the scheme barcode is captured. Certification against identification of eligible containers is Exchange for Change acting on barcoding: a machine that cannot read the registered EAN, UPC, Data Matrix or QR against the Article List cannot pay the deposit. Retailers who buy an uncertified machine now do so against a published list. That is the member risk.

Do not read the artwork guidance as an on-pack change. It is machine livery and consumer signage. Do not read certification as a new 2D duty. The RVM specification already required 2D Data Matrix and QR readability; this list confirms which families have passed the 77-test pack, including that read. Sunrise 2027 QR codes powered by GS1 remain an industry POS target, not a DRS legal requirement. If GS1 UK does nothing, retailers will buy from the PDF without asking whether the certified read includes GS1 Digital Link URIs or only linear EAN/UPC plus generic 2D, and producers will still lack the product-testing protocol promised for September. If members do nothing, they will specify an uncertified RVM, or a certified model whose Article List API and barcode-grade assumptions they have not tested against their own pack, and discover the failure at counting-centre or return-point trial rather than in artwork. Do not change GTINs on the back of this list. Do check any RVM you are procuring against the certified PDF, and keep pressing for the product-testing guidelines.
